front.title: The Sovereign AI Horizontal Memory (SAIHM) Protocol

abstract.t:
This document defines the Sovereign AI Horizontal Memory (SAIHM) protocol, a memory layer for AI agents. A SAIHM client seals every memory cell before it leaves the holder's machine, under a random data-encryption key that is wrapped under a key-encryption key only the client holds; the operator stores signed envelopes of ciphertext and wrapped keys and never holds a key able to decrypt them. The protocol specifies post-quantum identity binding (ML-DSA-65), authenticated sharing (ML-KEM-768), and cryptographic erasure by destruction of every operator-held copy of a cell's wrapped key, distinguished normatively from access-control erasure.
SAIHM lets agents that use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) persist, share, and erase memory across sessions, models, and vendors. It is intended to complement IETF work on agent dialog management and conversation data containers without overlapping it.
